about: Case file CF2 (cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost). Research text: the texts of the 'study' and 'event' timeline steps, 'boundary' (its lists) and each fact's 'what' are approved excerpt sentences (E3-E5, with their revisions after review), word for word; _tests/learn/test_cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost.js checks them. Study dates are the publishers' dates on Crossref (accessed 3 Nov 2026). 'idea' is an illustrative toy with invented round numbers, not the studies' inputs or results; its annual cost per MW, kilograms per MWh and variable cost are the stylized values of the allow-listed wind-hydrogen explainer (assets/explainers/wind-hydrogen.js).

boundary.title: Where the result holds
holds: one planned 253 MW wind farm in West Texas, with [[ercot|ERCOT]] wholesale prices;
hydrogen sold at a set price per kilogram;
leaves: final federal hydrogen credit rules, which came later;
the rest of the grid, which enters only through wholesale prices;
where the hydrogen goes after it is sold.
boundary.source: From the approved excerpt of Li et al. (2024), Journal of Mechanical Design.

idea.title: Your electrolyzer, one 10 MW block at a time
idea.note: Illustrative numbers, not the studies' inputs or results.
assumptions: free in this toy: it is surplus wind the grid cannot take, which would otherwise be curtailed
fewer for each added block: it runs only when the surplus is larger than the blocks below it

facts.what: Compared with wind and a battery alone, adding an electrolyzer reduced total system cost by about 7%, and using hydrogen as the storage medium for fuel cells reduced it by about 26%.
facts.source: Li et al. (2024), Journal of Mechanical Design

facts.what: The saving applies to the turbines alone, so its effect on the whole system was smaller: the levelized cost of hydrogen fell by about 2%.
facts.source: Li et al. (2024), J. Phys.: Conf. Ser. 2767
